incidents.victim: Czech Republic and Taiwan government, academic, technology and financial organizations
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails delivered a ZIP archive whose LNK or Rust-based dropper installed the Rustcloak loader and Azureveil C2 agent, which uses Azure Blob Storage as a dead-drop channel.
incidents.impact: Operation Dragon Weave is exfiltrating data from high-value targets aligned with Chinese intelligence priorities; researchers attribute the campaign to China with moderate confidence and assess the activity is ongoing.

incidents.victim: Thousands of compromised legitimate websites (Windows and macOS visitors)
incidents.vector: Attackers injected obfuscated JavaScript on thousands of legitimate sites, routing visitors through a zTDS traffic distribution system to FakeUpdate browser-update lures and ClickFix PowerShell paste lures that install malware.
incidents.impact: Silent Push describes 'DriveSurge' as a pay-per-install initial access broker operation that has hijacked thousands of trusted sites and gone undetected for nearly a year, selling access to downstream ransomware and malware crews.

incidents.victim: macOS users worldwide (Anglophone and Western European focus)
incidents.vector: Google Ads malvertising delivered notarized macOS applications (podcast player, PDF viewers) embedding the Flutter-based FlutterShell backdoor, which loads its logic dynamically from an attacker-controlled WebView bridge.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 says Operation FlutterBridge installs adware that hijacks Chrome traffic and gives operators arbitrary command execution, file system manipulation and environment-variable exfiltration; the malware was undetected on VirusTotal at first observation.

incidents.victim: Red Hat (@redhat-cloud-services npm namespace) and downstream enterprises
incidents.vector: A compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account pushed malicious orphan commits into RedHatInsights repositories, triggering the legitimate GitHub Actions OIDC publishing workflow to release 32 trojanized packages (~117K weekly downloads) carrying valid SLSA provenance and the 'Miasma' preinstall dropper.
incidents.impact: The Miasma payload (a Mini Shai-Hulud variant tied to TeamPCP tradecraft) harvests credentials for GitHub, npm, AWS, Azure, GCP, Vault and Kubernetes, scrapes GitHub Actions runner memory, escalates privileges and self-propagates by republishing maintainer packages with forged provenance; Red Hat pulled the packages and npm hardened the namespace.

incidents.victim: Instagram users including the Obama White House and U.S. Space Force Chief Master Sergeant accounts
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers used a VPN matching the target's home region to request a password reset, then social-engineered Meta's AI customer-support assistant into linking the account to an attacker-controlled email and issuing a one-time reset code.
incidents.impact: High-profile Instagram accounts were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian imagery and short 'value' handles allegedly worth more than $500,000 were hijacked; Meta confirmed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached, and accounts with MFA were unaffected.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a smart-contract flaw in the Gravity Bridge crypto bridge that moves assets between the Ethereum and Cosmos blockchains.
incidents.impact: Roughly $5.4 million in crypto assets were drained from the bridge; the company halted trading over the weekend to investigate.

incidents.vector: Compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to query land and real-estate data were abused to access the state registry.
incidents.impact: Approximately 600,000 records containing real names, cadastral information and other property-specific details were exfiltrated from Lithuania's state registry.

incidents.vector: Initial access vector has not been disclosed by Vietnamese investigators.
incidents.impact: Two unnamed Vietnamese agencies that store the personal data of millions of citizens were breached; the intrusions initially went undetected and Vietnamese authorities have opened an investigation.

incidents.vector: Specific intrusion vector not disclosed; Charter confirmed the breach after its name appeared on the ShinyHunters dark-web leak portal.
incidents.impact: American telecom Charter confirmed a data breach and is now listed by the ShinyHunters extortion crew, raising the prospect of customer data exposure as the group attempts to pressure the company.

Hackers stole medical data and biometric information including fingerprints and palm prints on at least 1.8 million people; because biometric identifiers cannot be replaced, the long-tail impact on affected individuals is severe.

incidents.vector: Initial access not disclosed; the Play ransomware group claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network.
incidents.impact: The Play ransomware group is extorting MyPillow and claims to hold sensitive financial documents; the company has not yet publicly confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Attackers laterally moved onto a senior finance executive's workstation, installed implants masquerading as Adobe and OneDrive components, used scheduled tasks for persistence, and exfiltrated mailbox contents via Dropbox using a legitimate .NET library from Aspose to convert emails to local files.
incidents.impact: Symantec and Carbon Black reported the attacker had near-continuous read access to the executive's Microsoft Outlook mailbox for at least five months (Aug 2025 - Feb 2026), exposing months of non-public information about listings, enforcement actions, and other market-moving exchange business; researchers say the attacker likely lost access after Mar 19, 2026.
sources: Symantec/Carbon Black Threat Hunter Team (via Dark Reading)

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with administrative access to the agency's code development platform created a public GitHub account ('Private-CISA') and disabled GitHub's built-in secret-protection, publishing plaintext credentials for dozens of internal CISA systems including AWS GovCloud keys.
incidents.impact: Sensitive CISA credentials - including an RSA key granting full access to all CISA-IT GitHub repositories - were exposed publicly from November 2025 until May 2026; CISA is still rotating credentials, and congressional lawmakers have demanded answers about controls at the agency that protects federal networks.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries / WorkTitans / MIRhosting infrastructure (used against EU targets)
incidents.vector: Dutch financial crime investigators (FIOD) raided three businesses and two data centers, arresting the co-owners of WorkTitans BV and MIRhosting for violating EU sanctions law by providing infrastructure to sanctioned Russian entities including PQHosting and Stark Industries.
incidents.impact: Authorities seized more than 800 servers used to launch DDoS attacks, disinformation campaigns and other cyberattacks against European targets (including pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies around the November 2025 municipal elections); customer data on the seized servers has been lost, disrupting an ecosystem of Kremlin-aligned operators.
